canonical_statement: The study evaluates whether reinforcement learning can teach language models to recognize underspecified reasoning problems and respond by asking for missing information, conditioning on unknowns, or abstaining instead of fabricating a definite answer.
ACA-RL training uses 120,000 generated missing-premise instances with localized gap annotations.
The Missing-Premise Benchmark contains 274 held-out, human-verified missing-premise instances spanning mathematical, logical, and real-world word problems.

The synthesis pipeline deconstructs a well-posed problem into background, conditions, question, and a reasoning DAG; perturbs a critical condition on the solution path; then rewrites and rechecks the result for plausibility and unanswerability.

Table 8 describes condition-breaking operations for missing-premise construction, including relationship removal, unquantifiable relationship replacement, numerical-value removal, qualifier removal, qualifier disruption, entity disruption, and condition contraction.
An LLM-based quality filter checks reasoning-graph correctness and missing-premise unanswerability and discards candidates that fail either check.
Against 556 human-annotated held-out candidates, the unanswerability filter achieved 93.0% accuracy.

canonical_statement: The behavioral taxonomy has five terminal response categories: silent hallucination, explicit assumption, abstention, conditional formulation, and active elicitation.

outcome.definition: Five-category classification of terminal response behavior

canonical_statement: ACA-RL assigns rewards of 1.0 for active elicitation, 0.6 for conditional formulation, 0.3 for abstention, -0.3 for explicit assumption, and -1.0 for silent hallucination.
Training-time reward assignment and MPB scoring use the same behavior taxonomy on separate instances; MPB is held out from the 120,000-instance ACA-RL training set.

The main comparison includes Cold-start SFT, Vanilla PPO trained only on well-posed answerable problems, IDK-RL trained for binary solve-or-refuse behavior, and ACA-RL with about 30% of its curated answerable queries transformed into missing-premise variants.
MPB responses are classified by GPT-5 into the five behavior categories and converted to a benchmark-level Behavior Score by averaging discrete per-response scores.
The experiments use Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, and Llama3.1-8B-Instruct; PPO is implemented with veRL, and the Qwen models receive a supervised cold start before RL.
The missing-premise training data are synthesized exclusively from DeepScaleR source questions.
Evaluation uses MPB, UMWP, and SUM for missing-premise or unanswerable behavior, plus GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024, LiveBench, and SciBench for well-posed capability checks.
MPB maps the five behavior categories to scores of 0, 25, 50, 75, and 100 for silent hallucination, explicit assumption, abstention, conditional formulation, and active elicitation, respectively.

outcome.definition: Discrete score mapped from terminal response category and averaged across instances

canonical_statement: The reported PPO configuration uses 4 nodes with 8 GPUs each, 400 total steps, actor and critic learning rates of 1e-6, mini-batch size 128, rollout temperature and top-p of 1.0, data batch size 512, and maximum response length 14,000.
Three graduate-level human experts performed a multi-stage MPB review that checked source and perturbed problem validity, gap-analysis accuracy, and overall quality after automated filtering.

The study uses LLMs for data synthesis, filtering, and GPT-based behavioral judging; the authors also state that general-purpose LLM writing assistants may have been used for minor wording, grammar, and formatting support.
The authors state that code, MPB, and training data are released with the work, but the inspected paper text does not provide a directly extractable repository URL.
On Qwen3-8B, ACA-RL achieved an MPB Behavior Score of 51.73 versus 48.72 for IDK-RL and 8.66 for Vanilla PPO.

outcome.definition: Average rubric-aligned score over held-out missing-premise instances

For Qwen3-8B on MATH-500, ACA-RL scored 92.60, compared with 93.40 for Vanilla PPO and 92.40 for IDK-RL.

Under the same data budget, reasoning-graph-guided synthesis produced an MPB score of 51.73, compared with 47.35 for SUM-derived data and 15.41 for Treecut-style perturbations.

canonical_statement: During the reported training-step sweep, MPB performance continued to rise while general reasoning benchmarks improved and then plateaued.
Across training, abstention appeared early, while conditional formulation and active elicitation increased more gradually and displaced some generic IDK responses.
Cold-start supervised fine-tuning improved ACA-RL learning efficiency and final MPB performance under the plotted training budget compared with no supervised warm start.
In the 10K, 20K, and 52K data-size sweep, larger generated datasets improved later-stage GSM8K and MPB performance, but the authors state that this does not establish a full scaling law.
Human experts agreed with the GPT-based behavior judge on approximately 98% of sampled GPT-5 responses.

canonical_statement: Active elicitation is evaluated only as a single-turn textual response; the method does not train retrieval, tool use, or multi-turn clarification policies that can acquire the missing premise.
The synthetic structural perturbations applied to logical problems may not capture the messy, implicit, or semantic ambiguity of organic user queries.

Training-time reward assignment and MPB scoring use the same behavior taxonomy; although MPB is held out, the authors call for independent scoring protocols and larger-scale human scoring, and margins over IDK-RL should be interpreted within the reported Behavior Score rubric.

The authors conclude that ACA-RL improves rubric-aligned missing-premise and unanswerable Behavior Scores across the tested model families while preserving competitive performance on the reported well-posed reasoning benchmarks.
The authors argue that reasoning systems should learn to recognize when missing information requires interaction, retrieval, or tool use instead of forcing a definite answer.
